answer: When k coordinated identities equivocate on the same consensus event, the protocol aggregates their attributable faults and applies a penalty proportional to k², rather than treating each bond in isolation. A sybil operator therefore risks an exponential multiplier in total capital loss upon detection as correlated penalties compound with asymmetric depreciation of slashed collateral. The inlet, reef, and raven labels may distinguish nodes, but cannot conceal shared evidence or evade aggregate enforcement.
